## State / SharedState

`State()` returns in-process state (local to the current process).  
`SharedState()` returns storage-backed state intended for prefork/multi-process sharing.

```go title="Signature"
func (app *App) State() *State
func (app *App) SharedState() *SharedState
```

See [State Management](./state.md) for usage and examples.

| <Reference id="sharedstorage">SharedStorage</Reference> | `Storage` | Storage behind [`SharedState`](./state.md#sharedstate-prefork-safe), which prefork workers and other processes can share when the storage itself is shared. The `SharedState` methods return `ErrSharedStorageNotConfigured` while it is `nil`. Fiber closes it on shutdown, after the services are terminated. | `nil` |
| <Reference id="skipunmatchedroutes">SkipUnmatchedRoutes</Reference>                   | `bool`                                                          | When enabled, requests whose path and method match no registered route are answered with `404` (or `405` when the path exists for other methods) before the middleware chain runs, avoiding work on requests to unregistered paths (bots, scanners, bad URLs). Warning: middleware never runs for skipped requests, so Use-based responders on unregistered paths (catch-all 404 pages, static, proxy, healthcheck, rewrite/redirect middleware) and logger/metrics visibility stop working for them. Rate limiters are in the same position: requests to unregistered paths are neither counted nor throttled, and leave no trace in the access log. CORS preflight requests are exempt so cors middleware keeps working. Customize the responses via `ErrorHandler`. With more than 64 entries in `RequestMethods` the option has no effect and requests go through the normal router.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `false`                                                                |
| <Reference id="streamrequestbody">StreamRequestBody</Reference>                       | `bool`                                                          | StreamRequestBody enables request body streaming, and calls the handler sooner when given body is larger than the current limit. Only [`Ctx.BodyStream()`](./ctx.md#bodystream) reads such a body: [`Ctx.Body()`](./ctx.md#body), [`Ctx.FormValue()`](./ctx.md#formvalue), the [body binders](./bind.md) and `net/http` handlers still refuse one larger than [`BodyLimit`](#bodylimit), and a multipart form is not parsed before the handlers run, as if `DisablePreParseMultipartForm` were set.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `false`                                                                |
| <Reference id="strictrouting">StrictRouting</Reference>                               | `bool`                                                          | When enabled, the router treats `/foo` and `/foo/` as different, for parametric routes such as `/users/:id/` as well. Otherwise, the router treats `/foo` and `/foo/` as the same. Prefixes are exempt: middleware registered with `Use` on `/foo/` also runs for `/foo`, which routes below it such as `/foo/:id?` and `/foo/*` answer, except for the wildcard prefixes [Routing](../guide/routing.md#parameters) names.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `false`                                                                |
